claims.statement: Mota owns its Google login end to end: an authorization-code + PKCE flow against the shared Supabase project coordinated by the API itself, because the shared auth-gateway keeps host-only session cookies that never reach mota's origin, so mota exchanges the one-time login code for its own host-only cookies instead of forwarding gateway cookies.

GET /api/auth/google validates the optional return_to query as a same-site path (must start with / and not //, otherwise HTTP 400 with no state created), generates the PKCE verifier and OAuth state, writes three flow cookies, and returns a 302 to ${SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/authorize carrying provider=google, prompt=select_account, redirect_to=${PUBLIC_URL}/api/auth/callback?state=<state>, code_challenge, and code_challenge_method=S256.
prompt=select_account is set on the authorize URL so Google always shows its account chooser instead of silently reusing the previously used Google identity on the shared Supabase project.

PKCE material is generated in-process: the code verifier and the OAuth state are each randomBytes(32) encoded as base64url (43 characters), and the code challenge is the base64url-encoded SHA-256 digest of the verifier; the S256 derivation is pinned against the RFC 7636 appendix B test vector.

GET /api/auth/callback requires a code query param, a state query param, the flow verifier cookie, and the flow state cookie; if any is missing or the state does not equal the cookie state under a length-check plus crypto.timingSafeEqual comparison, all three flow cookies are cleared and the request fails with 401 AUTH_CALLBACK_INVALID.

During the callback code exchange a SupabaseAuthError (provider definitively rejected) clears the flow cookies and becomes 401 AUTH_CALLBACK_INVALID, while any other error from exchangeCode — including SupabaseUnavailableError from a failed fetch or the 10-second timeout — is rethrown without clearing the flow cookies, so a Supabase outage does not burn the in-flight login.

A successful callback replies with five set-cookie headers: three that expire the flow cookies (Max-Age=0) and the two session cookies; the redirect target is the mota-return-url cookie value when it is still a same-site path, otherwise /, so a tampered return cookie cannot produce a cross-site redirect.

All auth cookies are host-only: HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Secure when the origin is https, and never a Domain attribute; the __Host- name prefix is applied only when PUBLIC_URL is an https origin, with unprefixed names over plain HTTP.

Cookie lifetimes: the access cookie's Max-Age is the Supabase session expires_in, the refresh cookie gets a fixed 30-day Max-Age (2,592,000 seconds), and each of the three flow cookies gets a 600-second Max-Age.

verifySupabaseSession's precedence is strict: a locally verified valid access token returns the AuthUser with no network call; otherwise, when a refresh cookie exists, the session is rotated server-side via the refresh grant and the fresh cookie strings are relayed through the optional onSetCookie callback before the new token is verified; SupabaseAuthError from the refresh yields null, while SupabaseUnavailableError propagates.

Refresh rotation has no dedicated endpoint: controllers pass an onSetCookie callback that calls reply.header('set-cookie', [...cookies]) — in AuthController.session and SettingsController.requireUser — so an ordinary request such as GET /api/auth/session or GET /api/settings can rotate the session and return fresh cookies alongside its payload.

A freshly refreshed access token that fails local verification throws SupabaseUnavailableError rather than returning null, because a token minted seconds ago should verify; this treats it as broken infrastructure, not as an anonymous user.

verifyAccessToken enforces local verification with no per-request gateway call: ES256 only, issuer ${supabaseUrl}/auth/v1 (derived from the same base URL the client uses), audience 'authenticated', a literal role claim of 'authenticated', a required non-empty sub, an optional valid email, and 5 seconds of clock tolerance; the JWKS resolver is created once per JWKS URL for the process lifetime and cached in a module-level Map.

In verifyAccessToken any jose error (code starting with ERR_, covering expired, forged, wrong-audience and JWKS-miss cases) returns null, while non-jose failures such as a refused JWKS connection throw SupabaseUnavailableError.

The verdict is translated per controller: a null user is 200 { authenticated: false } on /api/auth/session (anonymous is a normal state) but 401 AUTH_REQUIRED on /api/settings, while SupabaseUnavailableError always becomes 503 AUTH_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE with the same Korean message in both controllers.

POST /api/auth/logout clears both session cookies first (two Max-Age=0 set-cookie headers) and only then calls the Supabase signout endpoint, and only when both access and refresh cookies were present; every revoke failure is swallowed so a Supabase outage can never fail logout — the worst case is a Supabase-side session outliving the cookies.
An anonymous logout (no session cookies) still returns 200 { status: 'ok' } with the two clearing headers and makes no call to Supabase.

The web useAuthSession hook probes GET /api/auth/session once on mount with credentials 'include' and an 8-second abort, parses the body with authSessionResponseSchema, and distinguishes a genuinely anonymous visitor (authenticated false, error null) from a failed session check (authenticated false with the Korean error message).

useAuthSession.logout() sets the anonymous session state synchronously before awaiting POST /api/auth/logout, so the UI flips to anonymous before the round trip completes; a failed POST is swallowed and the session may be restored on the next load.

The GoogleLogin control renders three states — '로그인 확인 중' while the session check is in flight, an account chip with the verified email (falling back to '로그인됨') plus a logout button, or a 'Google로 로그인' link to /api/auth/google?return_to= the URL-encoded current path and query so login returns to the view the user left.

Configuration: SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_ANON_KEY are required by the Zod env schema, PUBLIC_URL defaults to http://localhost:5173, and trailing slashes are stripped from both supabaseUrl and publicUrl so the issuer, JWKS URL, and redirect_to callback are canonical; compose.yaml sets PUBLIC_URL to https://mota.m16khb.xyz in production, selecting the __Host- prefixes.

When AppModule.register is given no oauthConfig, AUTH_CONFIG is null and OAuthController.requireConfig turns every login attempt into 503 AUTH_NOT_CONFIGURED, and SESSION_VERIFIER falls back to a verifier that throws 'Supabase auth is not configured.' — so unconfigured deployments never expose a half-working login.

Every SupabaseAuthClient call (PKCE exchange, refresh, signout) posts to the Supabase token/signout endpoints with the anonKey as the apikey header and an AbortSignal.timeout of 10 seconds; there is no retry or backoff, a fetch rejection becomes SupabaseUnavailableError, and a non-OK response or a body failing the strict Zod session schema (access_token, refresh_token, positive integer expires_in, token_type) becomes SupabaseAuthError.

The OAuth callback URL ${PUBLIC_URL}/api/auth/callback must be allow-listed in the Supabase project's URL configuration, so changing the deployment origin without updating that allow-list breaks login at the provider step rather than inside mota's code.

The identity object that crosses the auth boundary is only { sub, email? } from packages/contracts/src/auth.ts; controllers never see the raw token or any other Supabase claim, and mota stores no duplicate user record.

The auth e2e suite drives the real Nest module against a loopback fake Supabase with a real ES256 keypair and pins the full contract: anonymous probes, local JWKS verification, 503 AUTH_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE instead of an anonymous body when fetch throws, expired access tokens treated as anonymous, the authorize redirect parameters plus three Max-Age=600 HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookies with no Domain attribute, 400 for cross-site return_to, five callback cookies with the refresh cookie at Max-Age=2592000, 401 for a forged state, logout clearing cookies and recording the signout, and refresh-only requests returning rotated session cookies.
The PWA service worker returns early for any /api/ pathname, so session probes, the OAuth callback, and logout always bypass the cache and reach the network.
